narrative:
The model estimates a 63% chance that you will leave your current job, which is why your promotion request has been denied. This prediction is driven primarily by three key factors about your situation.

The strongest influence is that you have received other job opportunities while working here. Having external offers is a major signal that you may be considering leaving, and this factor pushed the prediction most strongly toward departure.

Next, your six to ten years of experience in this organization worked in your favor. Employees predicted to stay often have shorter tenures in their current role, so your relatively long service here pulled the prediction back toward staying, though not enough to overcome the other signals.

Your overall career experience of six to ten years also contributed to the decision. While many employees predicted to stay have only one to five years of total experience, your broader background slightly increased the likelihood of leaving, perhaps because it gives you more options outside this company.

Taken together, these elements suggest the organization sees you as someone with attractive alternatives and enough experience to act on them. You and your manager should discuss ways to strengthen your connection to this workplace, such as exploring new internal opportunities or addressing any unmet needs, before external offers become too compelling.
